answers.A:
The per-period totals live in the `gltotals` table (one row per account and period). An AFTER INSERT trigger on `gltrans` (`gltrans_after_insert`) upserts into it, adding `NEW.amount` to the matching account/period row. Update and delete triggers (`gltrans_after_update`, `gltrans_after_delete`) also exist, created by update script 17, which seeded `gltotals` from `SUM(gltrans.amount)`. The material doesn't show what those two triggers do.

To get a balance, reports call `GetGLAccountBalance($AccountCode, $PeriodNo)` in `includes/GLFunctions.php`, which sums `gltotals.amount` for the account where `period <= $PeriodNo`. Some reports query `gltotals` directly instead, for example the balance sheet and cash flow reports. The account inquiry and report pages compute a running total from `gltotals` for periods before the first selected period.
answers.B:
The material doesn't say how the `gltotals` per-period totals are kept in step with GL transactions (for example, what updates them when `gltrans` rows are inserted), so on that part the answer is unknown. It only shows that `gltrans` rows are inserted with a `periodno`, as in the credit note API code.

For reading a balance, `GetGLAccountBalance($AccountCode, $PeriodNo)` in `includes/GLFunctions.php` runs `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM gltotals WHERE account=… AND period <= PeriodNo` and returns 0 if the result is null. Reports such as the GL account inquiry, cash flow and horizontal position pages sum `gltotals.amount` by period directly to get opening and closing balances. One report also flags an integrity problem when `ABS(PeriodTotal - PeriodActual)` exceeds `CurrencyTolerance`.
answers.none:
In webERP, every posting to `gltrans` also updates the `chartdetails` table, which holds one row per account per period. Code that inserts GL rows (invoices, receipts, journals, etc.) adds the amount to that period's `actual` figure, and for balance sheet accounts it also adjusts the `bfwd` (brought-forward) figures of later periods, so the totals stay in step with the transactions. Reports such as the trial balance, balance sheet and income statement read `chartdetails` instead of summing `gltrans`. They take `bfwd + actual` for a period, or `actual` summed over the periods in range for profit and loss accounts.

I'm answering from memory of the webERP schema, not from files here, so the details of which scripts do the updating are not verified.

answers.A:
When an order is created, the code compares the order value to the user's authority level in `purchorderauth` for the supplier's currency. If the user lacks authority (no row set up, or `authlevel` too low), the user gets a warning and the order is created with status `Pending` and printing is disallowed ([1], [2], [3], [4]). The material doesn't show the branch that sets `Authorised`, though it implies that happens when the user's limit covers the order.

Later, a user can authorise it through the status update on the order modification page if their `purchorderauth.authlevel` is greater than the order total; otherwise they get "You do not have permission to authorise this purchase order" [7]. Only `Authorised` or `Printed` orders can be printed [8].
answers.B:
A new purchase order is created as Authorised only if the user has authority for it. That means a `purchorderauth.authlevel` for the supplier's currency that exceeds the order value, and for the auto-placed orders from sales orders, `AutoAuthorisePO` must also be 1 [10]. Otherwise the user gets a warning and the order is created as Pending, with printing disallowed (`AllowPrintPO=0`) [1][3][4]. The warning says either that the user's authority hasn't been set up or that they can only authorise up to a given amount [1][2].

Later, someone can move it to Authorised in `PO_Header.php` if their `purchorderauth.authlevel` is greater than the order total [7][8]. Only Authorised or Printed orders can be printed [6].

answers.A: Each page script sets a `$PageSecurity` value before `header.php` is included, and the bootstrap checks it against the user's allowed tokens. If `!in_array($PageSecurity, AllowedPageSecurityTokens)`, the user gets a permission error [4]. Users belong to an Access Level or Security Group, which determines the tokens they hold, and a system admin can modify those group definitions under setup [2][5]. Some pages also add their own token checks, e.g. token 19 in `InternalStockRequestInquiry.php` [8].
answers.B: Each webERP script has a Page Security Level, which is a Security Token the user must hold to run it. Users get tokens through their Security Role (each user is allocated to a security group/role), and the session keeps them in `$_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']`. The session script (`session.php`) checks that an authorized user is logged in and that the page's security requirement is met. The levels can be edited under Main Menu > Setup > General > Page Security Settings. Pages can also use the same tokens in-page to control which data, buttons and links they show (e.g. `InternalStockRequestInquiry.php` checks for token 19).

The session include then checks that the logged-in user's token set contains that page's value, and if not, it shows a "not authorised" message and stops. After you log in, `includes/session.php` compares the code's `$Version` with the database's `VersionNumber` and starts the upgrade when the code is newer (material [1]). It also does a `HighestFileName` check against the numbered update scripts in `sql/updates/`, then redirects (material [2]). The README says that if any database upgrades are required, you are prompted to install them after login (material [5]).

The numbered updates are applied by `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`. It includes each `sql/updates/N.php`, runs the SQL through `executeSQL`, and records progress with `updateDBNo`, which sets `DBUpdateNumber` in the `config` table (material [4]). The main upgrade page, `UpgradeDatabase.php`, maps versions to scripts (material [3]).

The material doesn't spell out the comparison, but `HighestFileName` is presumably the highest-numbered file in `sql/updates/`, checked against the `DBUpdateNumber` config value that `GetConfig.php` loads. `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` then runs the numbered `sql/updates/N.php` scripts through `executeSQL` and `updateDBNo`. Each script records itself via `UpdateDBNo`, which updates `DBUpdateNumber`, and does so only if there were no errors. Tim notes the updates can't be run from outside webERP, since it is designed to control its own updating.
answers.none: From what I remember of webERP (I haven't checked this against your checkout), the `config` table holds a `DBUpdateNumber` value, which records the last database update applied. The code ships numbered update steps, defined in `includes/UpgradeDB_*.inc`, and the number the code expects is compared with the stored one. On login, `session.php` notices the mismatch and runs the pending steps in order, bumping `DBUpdateNumber` after each. I'm not sure of the exact file names or whether a manual page, such as `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`, also triggers it, so treat those details as unverified.

For each currency other than the company's default, the rate is set from the feed's rates through `GetCurrencyRate(currency, rates)`. The default currency is skipped, and the last-update date is then stored in the config [4]. The material does not say how `GetCurrencyRate` computes the value, so that part is unknown.

Each currency's rate comes from the configured feed, either the European Central Bank or DXR, and is looked up by currency code in the returned array [4][5]. A currency missing from the feed gets 0, and a rate of 0 is then treated as 1 [5]. The material doesn't say how a feed rate is converted into the stored rate beyond that.
answers.none: They don't run on a timer or cron job. The rates come from the European Central Bank feed, which is quoted against the euro. For each currency other than the home currency, the code sets the rate from the ECB figure, divided by the home currency's ECB rate when the home currency isn't EUR. It then stores today's date as the last-update date. I'm recalling this from memory of the code, so the exact function names are less certain than the overall behavior.

Goods are received at the purchase order price, converted to the home currency at the order's exchange rate. Under standard costing the stock is carried at standard cost, and the difference between the PO price and standard goes to the purchase price variance account.

When GL integration for stock is on, receipt debits the stock account of the item's category and credits the GRN suspense (clearing) account. The creditors ledger isn't touched at this point. The later supplier invoice match debits GRN suspense and credits creditors control, with any price difference going to variance.
